summary: iter95bm backend negotiation_mode tests: 17/17 PASS after fixing one persistence bug in create_price_book. All required scenarios validated: negotiation_mode toggle persistence + /template readback, auto price_min for materials/equipment (incl. MAX(line, book) rule), labor min/max copy from cennik, HTTP 400 block when below price_min with negotiation_mode=true (with PL message containing 'negocjacj'/'minimum'), allow + below_min=true history flag when negotiation_mode=false, below_min_accepted=true override, and price_book_id propagation on PATCH. Reference wycena (52438c80...) negotiation_mode restored to false. Regression suite (iter95bd) also passes (12/12).

fixed_during_testing.issue: PriceBookCreate model accepted price_min/price_max but the create_price_book endpoint did NOT include them in the MongoDB insert doc, so values were silently dropped. Caused MAX(unit, book_min) for materials/equipment and labor min/max copy from cennik to fail. Fixed by adding 'price_min'/'price_max' keys into the doc dict in /app/backend/routes/wyceny.py create_price_book().

IMPORTANT: the bug 'POST /api/wyceny/cennik silently dropped price_min/price_max' was fixed in this iteration — if future tests fail with cennik price fields missing, check that the doc dict in create_price_book() still includes these keys.
rca of the issue: RCA: PriceBookCreate Pydantic model (lines ~155-180) exposed price_min/price_max, but create_price_book() at lines ~644-686 built the insert doc manually without listing those two keys, so MongoDB stored them as missing. Reproduction: POST /api/wyceny/cennik with price_min=80 → GET cennik list → response has neither price_min nor price_max. Mitigation: explicit 'price_min': payload.price_min and 'price_max': payload.price_max added to the doc dict (between 'notes' and 'sub_category'). Long-term: switch to payload.dict(exclude_unset=False) or a serializer to avoid future drift between model and persisted shape.
